metadata.revision_notes: 0.2.0: verification pass on the two LAMC citations before implementation. LAMC Sec. 98.0602 content CORRECTED -- a more detailed, quote-like search result surfaced the actual figures (2-year total validity, 12-month expiration if work not commenced, 12-month continuous-abandonment expiration), which differ from 0.1.0-draft's incorrect '180 days' figure (likely conflated with a different jurisdiction's default ICC/IBC period). The '106.4.4.3 project inactivity, 90-day cure window' citation from 0.1.0-draft could NOT be verified on a second, more targeted attempt (not present in the LABC administration chapter fetched from up.codes; no independent confirmation found) and has been DROPPED rather than shipped as an unconfirmed specific legal claim. Also added: per-source verification_status, per-step grounding_strength, and one new specifically-keyed entry (pre_issuance_status_dwell x 'Corrections Issued') so lookup isn't category-generic-only.

entries.explanation: This status reflects a checkpoint in LADBS's plan check process. Depending on project complexity, permits are reviewed through different tracks -- Counter Plan Check and Express Permits for simpler projects, Expanded Counter Plan Check for modest projects like multi-floor tenant improvements or medium-sized additions, and Regular Plan Check for large or complex projects -- and processing checkpoints can take different amounts of time depending on the track and reviewer workload. Publicly available sources do not clearly document what specifically causes a permit to remain in most individual pre-issuance statuses for an extended time.

developer_actionable_steps.text: Contact LADBS or the assigned plan check engineer to ask what is needed to move this permit toward its next status.

city_dependent_steps.text: Advancing a permit past a plan-check review checkpoint is a LADBS-side action.

entries.explanation: LADBS issues a correction notice (referred to in LADBS's glossary as a 'G-49') when plan check review finds items that need to be revised before plans can be approved. The applicant is generally expected to review the circled corrections, revise the plans, and contact the plan check engineer for a verification appointment once corrections have been addressed. A permit remaining in 'Corrections Issued' status can indicate the applicant has not yet resubmitted revised plans, or that a resubmission is still awaiting the plan check engineer's re-review -- this data does not distinguish which.

developer_actionable_steps.text: Review the correction notice with the architect, engineer, or designer responsible for the plans.
Once revised plans address all circled corrections, contact the plan check engineer to schedule a verification appointment.

city_dependent_steps.text: Re-review of resubmitted plans is performed by the LADBS plan check engineer.

entries.explanation: LADBS expects a permit holder to schedule and pass inspections for each phase of a project before moving on to the next one, starting once the permit is issued and construction begins. A long gap between issuance and the first recorded inspection can occur when construction hasn't reached an inspectable stage yet, when the first inspection hasn't been requested, or for reasons not visible in this data.

developer_actionable_steps.text: If construction has reached an inspectable stage, request the applicable inspection through LADBS's inspection request service.
Confirm the permit and approved plans will be available on-site, as required for inspections.

city_dependent_steps.text: Inspection scheduling and availability are managed by LADBS.

entries.explanation: Under LAMC Sec. 98.0602, a permit is generally valid for two years from issuance, but expires 12 months from issuance if the authorized work has not commenced, and also expires if the Department determines the work has been suspended, discontinued, or abandoned for a continuous period of 12 months. Extensions may be available -- for residential permits, the code provides for extensions where unusual construction difficulties are shown to have prevented work from starting or continuing.

developer_actionable_steps.text: If work has not yet commenced, be aware the permit may expire 12 months after issuance under LAMC Sec. 98.0602 -- consider starting inspectable work or requesting an extension before that window closes.
If unusual construction difficulties have prevented starting or continuing work, ask LADBS about requesting an extension.

city_dependent_steps.text: LADBS determines whether a permit has expired due to non-commencement or abandonment, and decides on extension requests.

entries.explanation: LADBS expects a permit holder to schedule and pass inspections for each phase of a project before moving on to the next one. A long gap between two recorded inspections can occur when construction work between phases is slower than typical, when the next inspection hasn't been requested yet, or for reasons not visible in this data.

developer_actionable_steps.text: If the next phase of work is ready, request the next inspection through LADBS's inspection request service.
Confirm the permit and approved plans are available on-site, as required for each inspection.

city_dependent_steps.text: Inspection scheduling and availability are managed by LADBS; scheduling windows and any backlog are outside the applicant's control.

entries.explanation: Under LAMC Sec. 98.0602, a permit expires if the Department determines the authorized work has been suspended, discontinued, or abandoned for a continuous period of 12 months. An open-ended gap since the most recent recorded inspection can indicate the project is between phases, that the next inspection hasn't been requested, or that the project has become inactive.

developer_actionable_steps.text: Request the next applicable inspection to demonstrate the project remains active and reduce risk of the permit being treated as abandoned under LAMC Sec. 98.0602.

city_dependent_steps.text: Inspection scheduling, and any determination that work has been suspended, discontinued, or abandoned, are managed by LADBS.

entries.explanation: Before LADBS will schedule a final building inspection for a Certificate of Occupancy, other trade permits on the project (electrical, plumbing, mechanical, etc.) generally need to be finaled first, and multiple agencies' sub-final inspections (building, fire/life safety, accessibility, energy compliance, and others as applicable) are typically coordinated together. A gap between the last recorded substantive inspection and Certificate of Occupancy issuance can reflect this multi-trade coordination, additional required inspections not captured as 'substantive' in this data, or other reasons not visible here.

developer_actionable_steps.text: Confirm all other trade permits (electrical, plumbing, mechanical, etc.) on this project have been finaled.
Request the general building final inspection once all sub-finals are complete.

city_dependent_steps.text: Issuing the Certificate of Occupancy, and verifying permit history for unpermitted work, is a LADBS action.

entries.explanation: LADBS issues an Inspection Correction Notice when a site inspection finds items that need to be fixed before the work can be approved. After addressing plan-check corrections, the applicant is generally expected to contact the plan check engineer for a verification appointment. Repeated correction cycles are generally associated with recurring compliance issues that take more than one inspection visit to resolve.

developer_actionable_steps.text: Review each Inspection Correction Notice with the contractor or tradesperson responsible for that item before requesting reinspection.
Contact the plan check engineer for a verification appointment once corrections have been addressed.

city_dependent_steps.text: Reinspection to confirm a correction has been resolved requires LADBS to visit the site again.
